History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has had wheezing for the past 2–3 days.
Patient reports no fever and has recorded a temperature of 37 °C.
Patient is not coughing up sputum.
Patient denies haemoptysis or chest pain.
Patient is not waking at night because of symptoms.
Sometimes the patient cannot complete sentences, but has no shortness of breath at rest.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sometimes can't complete sentences but no SOB at rest

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has no problems walking upstairs.
Wheezing is worse when walking to work.
Patient does not have a peak-flow meter at home.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Doesn't have peak flow meter at home.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has missed a few days of work because of symptoms.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Has missed a few days of work.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of asthma since childhood.
Patient had hospital admissions for asthma but no intensive-care stays.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Had hospital admissions and missed school. No ITU.

Medications.content: Patient intermittently uses a salbutamol inhaler every few weeks.
Medications.source_text: sometimes takes salbutamol still every few weeks

Medications.content: Patient stopped regular asthma medication 3–4 years ago.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks about 1 unit of alcohol every 2–3 days.

Assessment.content: Clinical impression is an exacerbation of asthma.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient advised to continue monitoring temperature and contact the clinic if fever spikes.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Continue to monitor temperature and speak to us if spiking temperatures.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient to collect prescription for a peak-flow meter and spacer.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Collect prescription of peak flow meter and spacer.

Plan_of_Care.content: Pharmacist will advise the patient on how to use the peak-flow meter and spacer.
Patient should record peak expiratory flow rate twice daily, once on waking and at night.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Record PEFR twice daily, first on waking and at night.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase salbutamol with spacer to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Increase salbutamol with spacer to 2-4 puffs 4hrly

Plan_of_Care.content: A second inhaler may need to be added to the regimen.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: May need to add in another inhaler.

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient advised to take a regular antihistamine.

Follow_up_Information.content: Arrange a review appointment next week.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: arrange a review with us next week

Follow_up_Information.content: If wheeze is not settling or worsening and patient feels unwell, seek an urgent appointment.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: If wheeze not settling/getting worse in meantime if feels unwell for urgent appointment.
